chunks: Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-'Askari narrated to us, he said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Durayd narrated to us, he said: Abu Hatim informed us from al-'Utbi - meaning Muhammad ibn 'Ubaydallah - from his father, he said: And 'Abdullah ibn Shabib al-Basri informed us, he said: Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Munqari narrated to us, he said: Al-'Ala' ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, he said: Qays ibn 'Asim said:

I set out with a group from Bani Tamim to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So I entered, and al-Salsal ibn al-Dalhamas was with him. I said: 'O Prophet of God, admonish us with an admonition by which we may benefit, for we are a people who dwell in the wilderness.' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

'O Qays! Indeed with glory there is humiliation, and with life there is death, and with this world there is a Hereafter. For everything there is a reckoner, and over everything there is an observer. For every good deed there is a reward, and for every sin there is a punishment, and for every term there is a decree. And it is inevitable for you, O Qays, that you will have a companion who will be buried with you while it is alive, and you will be buried with it while you are dead. If it is noble, it will honor you; and if it is base, it will forsake you. Then it will not be gathered except with you, nor will you be resurrected except with it, nor will you be asked about anything except it. So make it nothing but righteous, for if it is righteous you will find comfort in it, and if it is corrupt you will find nothing but dread from it. And it is your deeds.'

He said: 'O Prophet of God, I would love for these words to be in verses of poetry, so we may take pride in them before those Arabs around us, and preserve them.' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ordered someone to bring Hassan. He said: I began reflecting on poetry that resembled this admonition, and the words came to me before Hassan arrived. I said: 'O Messenger of God, some verses have come to me which I think match what you want.' So I said to Qays:

'Choose a companion from your deeds, for indeed the companion of the youth in the grave is what he used to do. And after death you must surely prepare it for a day when the person is called and comes forward. If you are occupied with something, then do not be occupied with anything other than what pleases God. Man will not be accompanied after his death, nor before it, by anything except what he used to do. Indeed, man is but a guest of his family; he stays among them a little while, then departs.'

key_terms.البرية: The wilderness, desert -- indicating the nomadic Bedouin lifestyle of Bani Tamim
key_terms.قرين: Companion, associate -- here metaphorically referring to one's deeds that accompany a person to the grave
key_terms.موعظة: Admonition, religious counsel -- advice that softens the heart and leads to righteous action

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about deeds being a companion in the grave?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (s) admonished Qays ibn 'Asim, a Bedouin chief from Bani Tamim who visited him seeking guidance. The Prophet explained that one's deeds are a companion that accompanies a person into the grave and the afterlife -- if righteous, they bring honor; if corrupt, they bring desolation. When Qays asked for the teaching in poetic form to preserve among the Arabs, the narrator composed verses summarizing the lesson: man is a temporary guest in this world, and his only true companion is his deeds.
